public.about.ctaSub: Find what's happening in your city, or put your own event in front of it.
public.about.missionText: We enable anyone in Iraq to run an event and sell tickets to the audience it's meant for.
public.about.p1Body: From a workshop down the street to a festival in a stadium: publish your page, sell your tickets and check guests in at the door, all from one dashboard.
public.about.p2Body: We're working towards paying the way you already pay, knowing the refund policy before you spend a dinar, and holding your ticket the moment you buy it.
public.about.p3Body: We don't just sell your tickets. We put your event in front of the people in your city who actually care about it. Not everyone, but the audience you made it for.
public.about.p4Body: Baghdad first, then Erbil, Basra, Mosul, Najaf and Anbar. One city at a time, each one done properly.
public.about.storyP1: iEvent is an Iraqi platform for discovering events and booking tickets to them. We started in Baghdad with a simple idea: the best thing happening in your city shouldn't pass you by, and anyone who puts in the work to organise something worth attending deserves tools worth using.
public.about.storyP2: For organisers, we build a dashboard that runs everything, from publishing the page to checking guests in at the door. For attendees, a ticket you can trust and payment methods you already know. And between the two, a city with more life in it.
public.about.storyTitle: Started in Baghdad, built for every city
public.about.visionText: That every Iraqi knows what's happening in their city before they miss it.
public.help.a1a: Browse events by city, category, date and price, or start typing in the search box and matching events appear as suggestions. Save events you like with the heart, and follow organizers so their next event reaches you first.
public.help.a1q: How do I find events near me?
public.help.a2a: No. You can check out as a guest and we email your tickets. Creating an account keeps your order history and tickets in one place, and you can sign in with Google in one tap.
public.help.a2q: Do I need an account to buy a ticket?
public.help.a3a: Free events are instant: register and your tickets are issued on the spot. For paid events, you pay the organizer directly: transfer to the wallet or card shown at checkout and upload your receipt, or pay cash at the door where the organizer allows it. The organizer confirms your order, usually within a few hours. Online card and wallet payments inside checkout are on our roadmap.
public.help.a3q: How do I pay for tickets?
public.help.a4a: The moment your order is confirmed, your tickets are emailed to you as a PDF and appear under My tickets in your account. Each ticket has its own QR code, and you can download or print them anytime.
public.help.a5a: The organizer scans your ticket's QR code at entry. Each ticket admits one person and is voided once scanned, so it can't be reused. If tickets carry holder names, the organizer may check them against ID.
public.help.a6a: Every event page shows the organizer's refund policy before you pay a dinar. Refunds are issued by the organizer through the same method you paid with. If your order is refunded, its tickets are voided and you're notified by email.
public.help.a7a: You're emailed automatically the moment the organizer changes the date or cancels. On a postponement your tickets stay valid for the new date. For events whose date is still to be announced, follow the organizer and you'll hear the moment it's set.
public.help.a7q: What if the event is postponed or cancelled?
public.help.a8a: From Account settings you can update your name, phone, city and profile photo, pick the interests that shape your recommendations, and switch the site between Arabic and English at any time.
public.help.a8q: How do I manage my account?
public.help.attSub: Finding events, tickets, payments and what happens at the door.
public.help.o1a: Create your organizer profile in minutes, then the event wizard walks you through five steps: details, photos, tickets, extras and review. Your work is autosaved as a draft on the way, and nothing is public until you press Publish.
public.help.o1q: How do I publish my first event?
public.help.o2a: Nothing during the beta: no platform fees on any ticket, free or paid. After the beta, a small booking fee applies to paid tickets, published openly on our pricing page. Free events stay free forever.
public.help.o3a: Buyers pay you directly. Add your wallet or card details once, and buyers transfer to them at checkout and upload the receipt for you to confirm, or pay cash at the door if you enable it. Money never passes through iEvent.
public.help.o4a: Yes. An event can have an exact date, run across several days, show just a month and year, or say the date is still to be announced. Set the real date later and every ticket buyer is notified.
public.help.o4q: My event's date isn't fixed yet. Can I still publish?
public.help.o5a: Add up to 10 photos: upload your own or pick free stock photos from the built-in search. Star any image to make it the cover, adjust how each one is cropped, and two or more photos become a slideshow on your page.
public.help.o5q: How do photos and covers work?
public.help.o6a: Every event gets share links per channel that count their own clicks, discount codes for early birds and partners, and an embeddable ticket widget for your own website. Your page is automatically translated so both Arabic and English audiences can read it, and you can list it under up to 3 categories.
public.help.o6q: How do I promote my event?
public.help.o7a: Open Check-in on your phone and scan QR codes with the camera, or plug in any USB scanner. Each ticket is validated once, the live counter updates as guests arrive, and you can undo a scan if you need to.
public.help.o7q: How does check-in work at the door?
public.help.o8a: Yes. Invite teammates by email with the role you choose: full management access or check-in only. They accept the invite and appear in your team list, and you can remove them anytime.
public.help.o8q: Can my team help me run the event?
public.help.o9a: Both are one action from your event console. Every buyer is emailed automatically: on a postponement tickets stay valid for the new date, and on a cancellation you arrange refunds per your policy.
public.help.o9q: What if I need to postpone or cancel?
public.help.orgSub: Publishing your event, getting paid and running the door.
public.help.stillSub: Questions, issues or feedback. We read every message and reply by email.

public.meta.aboutDescription: iEvent is an Iraqi platform for discovering events and booking tickets. Our vision: every Iraqi knows what's happening in their city before they miss it.
public.meta.helpDescription: How iEvent works for attendees and organizers: finding events, buying tickets, payments, refunds, publishing events and check-in.
public.meta.pricingDescription: iEvent is free during the beta: no platform fees on any ticket. See exactly what the booking fee will be after that, published in advance.
public.pricing.afterSub: When the beta ends, a small booking fee will apply to paid tickets only. This is the exact formula, published now so there are no surprises later:
public.pricing.afterTitle: After the beta: simple, published in advance
public.pricing.ctaSub: Publish a beautiful event page in minutes. Free during the beta.
public.pricing.heroSub: iEvent is in beta, and during the beta everything is free: no platform fees on any ticket, paid or free. You keep the full ticket price.
public.pricing.inc3: Share links, discount codes and a website widget
public.pricing.inc5: Your page in Arabic and English
public.pricing.inc6: Direct payments and cash at the door
public.pricing.moneyBody: Buyers pay you directly: by transfer to your own wallet or card, or in cash at the door. Ticket money never passes through iEvent, and there is nothing to withdraw or wait for.
public.pricing.moneyTitle: Your money goes straight to you
public.pricing.promiseBody: Any change to pricing will be announced well in advance, in plain language, on this page. No hidden fees, no surprises.
public.pricing.whoPaysBody: Pass the booking fee to the buyer on top of the ticket price, or absorb it yourself so buyers pay exactly the price on the ticket. It's one switch on your event.
